protocol.status: Frozen before examining design comparison results; internal protocol, not external preregistration
protocol.question: At the same expected number of observed vertices, which of three roster-based independent sampling designs estimates the network closure contrast most precisely?
protocol.population: Simple undirected projection of SNAP email-Eu-core, using the complete department roster as auxiliary allocation information
protocol.estimand: D = 3 * triangles - 0.25 * wedges; sign agrees with transitivity minus 0.25 when wedges > 0
allocation_scores: inverse square root of department size
protocol.coupling: Common uniform vector across designs at a seed; independent vectors across seeds. Design comparisons are paired.
protocol.selection_rule: Minimize mean estimated variance of D in the pilot. Compare with minimizing the diagonal-only variance approximation. Hold both choices fixed before evaluation.
outcomes: exact design variance from the complete reference graph
evaluation empirical variance and mean squared error
paired bootstrap uncertainty for evaluation MSE ratio to uniform
mean selected vertices and induced edges
negative estimated variance and indefinite covariance counts
protocol.restrictions: Report all three designs. Do not tune allocation or threshold after seeing outcomes. No population confidence intervals, hypothesis-test significance, external adoption or original-collection validity claim. Node cost is equal in expectation, not exactly; induced-edge cost may differ. This is a reference-population design-planning case, not an optimal sampling algorithm.

interpretation: Bootstrap intervals quantify simulation uncertainty in the paired MSE ratio, not confidence intervals for the population contrast. Pilot and evaluation seeds are disjoint; designs share uniforms at each seed. Exact population values are validation oracles, not sample-accessible inputs.
